candidate_relations.reason: Ichthyosis vulgaris causes generalized scaling rather than folliculocentric lichen sclerosus with epidermal atrophy and homogenized papillary dermal collagen.
Darier disease does not match the hypopigmented atrophic papules or the characteristic lichen sclerosus histopathology.
Ichthyosis is a different diagnostic family and does not capture folliculocentric lichen sclerosus et atrophicus.
Sparse bandlike lymphocytes can be described as lichenoid inflammation, but lichenoid dermatitis does not identify the required folliculocentric lichen sclerosus diagnosis.
Pityriasis rubra pilaris may have follicular papules but lacks the clinical atrophy and homogenized papillary dermal collagen of lichen sclerosus.
Keratosis pilaris can be folliculocentric with plugs but does not account for epidermal atrophy and papillary dermal sclerosis characteristic of lichen sclerosus.
Scleroderma is not folliculocentric lichen sclerosus and is unsupported by the keratin-plugged atrophic papules and superficial homogenized collagen pattern.
Lichen planopilaris targets scalp follicles and causes cicatricial alopecia, unlike truncal folliculocentric lichen sclerosus.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Different lichenoid disease centered on hair follicles with scarring alopecia

candidate_relations.reason: Phrynoderma may cause follicular keratotic papules but does not produce the histologic sclerosis and epidermal atrophy of lichen sclerosus.
Lichen spinulosus produces grouped spiny follicular papules rather than atrophic hypopigmented lesions with lichen sclerosus histology.
Lichen planus is related only by lichenoid morphology; the follicular plugs, epidermal atrophy, and homogenized papillary dermal collagen support lichen sclerosus instead.
Dermatophytosis does not explain the chronic folliculocentric atrophic papules or lichen sclerosus histopathology.
Psoriasis lacks the folliculocentric keratin plugs, epidermal atrophy, and homogenized papillary dermal collagen seen here.
